bibliographic.title: LLM-Assisted Scoping Review of Artificial Intelligence in Brazilian Public Health: Lessons from Transfer and Federated Learning for Resource-Constrained Settings
bibliographic.authors: Fabiano Tonaco Borges; Gabriela do Manco Machado; Maíra Araújo de Santana; Karla Amorim Sancho; Giovanny Vinícius Araújo de França; Wellington Pinheiro dos Santos; Carlos Eduardo Gomes Siqueira
bibliographic.venue: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
bibliographic.citation_apa: Borges, F. T., Machado, G. M., de Santana, M. A., Sancho, K. A., de França, G. V. A., dos Santos, W. P., & Siqueira, C. E. G. (2026). LLM-Assisted Scoping Review of Artificial Intelligence in Brazilian Public Health: Lessons from Transfer and Federated Learning for Resource-Constrained Settings. International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health, 23(1), 81. https://doi.org/10.3390/ijerph23010081

methodology.method_family: scoping review with LLM-assisted title screening
methodology.sample_description: Literature retrieved from publicly accessible databases (PubMed, SciELO, and the CNPq Theses and Dissertations Repository); no new individual-level or confidential data were created or analyzed
methodology.sector: public health; Brazilian Unified Health System (SUS)
methodology.technology_context: artificial intelligence, machine learning, transfer learning, federated learning, foundation models, large language models in healthcare; resource-constrained and Global South health systems

eligibility.exclusion_reason: The article is a scoping review on AI applications in Brazilian public health with primary emphasis on transfer learning and federated learning in resource-constrained settings. LLMs appear as background context and as an assistive tool for title screening, not as the object of conversational governance analysis.
eligibility.decision_rationale: Although the title and screening hits include LLM, governance, healthcare, and compliance terms, the provided text shows the study objective is mapping AI use in the Brazilian SUS and examining transfer learning and federated learning for data scarcity, privacy, and infrastructure limits. ChatGPT is reported only for preliminary title classification in the review workflow. No evidence in the supplied text addresses conversational systems, chatbot/agent governance, guardrails, observability, human oversight of LLM interactions, or post-deployment conversational risk controls.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: High keyword overlap from automated screening (LLM, governance, healthcare) may overstate relevance; manual check needed to confirm LLM is methodological support rather than governance subject and that conversational AI is not substantively covered in unseen sections.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal is partial because only front matter, fragments, acknowledgments, and keyword hits were supplied. Within that material, the review objective and scoping design are clear, but full search strategy, inclusion criteria detail, screening counts, and synthesis procedures are not visible.

cerqual.explanation: For the review's target question on conversational governance of LLM-based systems, relevance is low: the study addresses public-health AI deployment patterns and federated/transfer learning governance aligned with data protection, not conversational AI accountability or operational controls.

coding.theme: AI adoption and privacy-preserving deployment models in Brazilian public health
coding.subtheme: Transfer and federated learning as governance-aligned alternatives to centralized high-resource AI

synthesis.main_claim: AI adoption in Brazilian healthcare is emerging but uneven; transfer learning and federated learning offer scalable, privacy-preserving pathways for clinically relevant tools in underserved, heterogeneous health systems.
synthesis.contribution: Maps AI application within the Brazilian Unified Health System and positions federated learning as a governance-aligned strategy consistent with data protection laws such as LGPD and national digital health sovereignty.
synthesis.use_in_review: Exclude as central or supporting evidence for conversational governance of LLM systems. May serve only as peripheral contextual background on federated-learning-based data governance and regulated public-health AI in Brazil if the review includes a separate thread on decentralized AI governance outside conversational systems.
